body:
**Estate audit EST-AUD-233**: severity **low**, dimension `security-k8s`, standard [STD-K8S-04](https://github.com/jvallery/agents/blob/main/docs/estate/STANDARDS.md#std-k8s-04)

## What needs to change
Add an Egress NetworkPolicy for component=mcp allowing DNS, verdify-db:5432, the planner-trigger path it needs, and public 443 for OpenAI only; give verdify-mcp a dedicated ServiceAccount with automountServiceAccountToken: false.

## Why it matters
It is the verdify workload most exposed to external callers; unrestricted egress turns any server bug into a pivot to the LAN and NAS.

## Evidence (live, 2026-10-19)
verdify-prod has default-deny-ingress and allow-mcp-internal/allow-web-tiers-from-verdify-traefik (Ingress only); none of the Egress-type policies in the namespace selects app.kubernetes.io/component=mcp, so the pod reaches any destination. It holds DB credentials (verdify-mcp-runtime-db), OPENAI_API_KEY and both MCP tokens. Pods run as SA 'default' with automountServiceAccountToken unset on both the pod and SA, so a token is mounted; kubectl auth can-i --list for system:serviceaccount:verdify-prod:default shows only discovery/kubevirt read verbs (low impact). Compare kepler-estate-boundary, which limits egress to DNS, observability, argocd-server, Proxmox/API IPs and public 443.

Affected: `k8s:verdify-prod/deployment/verdify-mcp`, `k8s:verdify-prod/networkpolicy (no Egress policy selects component=mcp)`, `k8s:verdify-prod/serviceaccount/default`

## Approach
Derive required destinations from the deployment env and a short Hubble/conntrack-free check of logs; write the policy in deploy/k8s/base, roll to prod via the normal sync, verify tools still answer.

## Alignment with best practice and estate rules
R20 network policy; verdify-platform owns its namespace.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] kubectl get networkpolicy shows an Egress policy selecting component=mcp
- [ ] A test pod-exec-free probe (e.g. tool call that hits DB and forecast) still succeeds
- [ ] Pod spec shows automountServiceAccountToken=false


_Filed by the 2026-10-19 estate best-practice gap audit. The finding was verified live by an independent re-check. Baseline: [docs/estate/STANDARDS.md](https://github.com/jvallery/agents/blob/main/docs/estate/STANDARDS.md); owner from the estate ownership record (jvallery/agents `registry/policy/estate-ownership/`)._

<!-- planning-status:start -->
## Planning status (2026-10-19)

### Status (2026-10-19)
Not started.
### Evidence
- default SA, token mounted; no mcp Egress policy (2026-10-19)
### Acceptance
- Satisfied: none yet
- Outstanding: Egress policy selecting component=mcp; tool call hitting DB/forecast still succeeds; automountServiceAccountToken=false
### Related work
#1007
### Dependencies
None.
### Priority & next action
P3: Add dedicated SA (automount false) and Egress policy in deploy/k8s/base; sync. Verify: pod spec readback; Hermes tool call succeeds.
### Standard
STD-K8S-04, STD-K8S-02, R20
### Triage (2026-10-20)
- Priority: **P3**. Egress and SA-token hardening for the MCP pod; low severity (default SA has only discovery verbs).
- Standards (corrected): STD-K8S-02
- Quality: STD-K8S-04 is default-deny ingress (already met); the egress gap has no exact standard—lead with STD-K8S-02 and R20.
<!-- planning-status:end -->

**Estate audit EST-AUD-232**: severity **low**, dimension `observability`, standard [STD-OBS-06](https://github.com/jvallery/agents/blob/main/docs/estate/STANDARDS.md#std-obs-06)

## What needs to change
Emit one structured event per allowed tool call (audience, tool, write/read class, result) and trust X-Forwarded-For/CF-Connecting-IP only from verdify-traefik so the access log shows the real client.

## Why it matters
With a public, token-authenticated MCP that can change setpoints, the success path is the one that needs attribution; denial-only logging cannot answer who changed a plan.

## Evidence (live, 2026-10-19)
kubectl logs on both verdify-mcp pods, last 24h: 7,918 'mcp_transport_authn_denial' and 2 'mcp_tool_authz_denial' JSON events carry audience/tool/reason, but the 627 successful POST /mcp lines are bare uvicorn access lines ('<ip> - POST /mcp 200') with no audience or tool. Source IPs are pod IPs only: 10.42.4.220 (verdify-hermes-iris) and 10.42.4.121/10.42.6.158 (verdify-traefik), so public callers' real addresses are lost (uvicorn runs without --proxy-headers/forwarded-allow-ips). set_plan/set_tunable writes therefore cannot be tied to a caller from logs.

Affected: `k8s:verdify-prod/deployment/verdify-mcp`, `VerdifyConsultancy/verdify-platform mcp/server.py`, `k8s:verdify-prod/deployment/verdify-traefik`

## Approach
In authorize_tool_call, log an 'mcp_tool_call' event on allow (reuse _TOOL_AUTH_LOGGER, never the token). Start uvicorn with proxy_headers=True and forwarded_allow_ips set to the verdify-traefik pod CIDR or use Traefik access logs with the CF header.

## Alignment with best practice and estate rules
R13; producer lane verdify-platform.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Loki {namespace="verdify-prod",app component mcp} shows mcp_tool_call events with audience and tool for Hermes calls
- [ ] A public test call shows the external client IP, not a verdify-traefik pod IP


_Filed by the 2026-10-19 estate best-practice gap audit. The finding was verified live by an independent re-check. Baseline: [docs/estate/STANDARDS.md](https://github.com/jvallery/agents/blob/main/docs/estate/STANDARDS.md); owner from the estate ownership record (jvallery/agents `registry/policy/estate-ownership/`)._

<!-- planning-status:start -->

### Status (2026-10-19)
Not started.
### Evidence
- Only denials attributed in logs (2026-10-19)
### Acceptance
- Satisfied: none yet
- Outstanding: mcp_tool_call events with audience/tool in Loki; public test call shows real client IP
### Related work
#1007
### Dependencies
None; helps #1007 caller identification.
### Priority & next action
P3: Log mcp_tool_call on allow in authorize_tool_call; run uvicorn with proxy headers trusted from verdify-traefik only. Verify: Loki query shows events; public call shows external IP.
### Standard
STD-OBS-06, R13
### Triage (2026-10-20)
- Priority: **P3**. Audit-trail gap for successful MCP calls; low severity, becomes less important if #1007 removes the public route.
- Standards (corrected): STD-EXP-01
- Quality: STD-OBS-06 is host/VM log shipping to Loki; this is application audit attribution—cite STD-EXP-01 context (public write-capable app) and note no exact standard.
<!-- planning-status:end -->

body:
**Estate audit EST-AUD-225**: severity **medium**, dimension `security-supply-chain`, standard [STD-CI-04](https://github.com/jvallery/agents/blob/main/docs/estate/STANDARDS.md#std-ci-04)

## What needs to change
Make OTA images verifiable end to end. Build from a pinned commit into the artifacts store with a signature and provenance. Flash only an artifact whose signature and SHA match the reviewed build, and have the device itself refuse unsigned images (ESP-IDF signed app verification or Secure Boot v2). Narrow the builder's egress, and restrict OTA tcp/3232 and API tcp/6053 on the device to the named builder and ingestor sources.

## Why it matters
The greenhouse controller drives live plant equipment: heaters, misters, fans and lights. Today, anyone who learns the one static OTA password, or anything that runs in a pod holding it, can push arbitrary firmware from any VLAN that can route to 192.168.10.111, including the home LAN. The builder flashes whatever `main` resolves to at run time, built with internet-fetched toolchain packages, so a bad push to main or a compromised dependency reaches the device with no signature or review step. The archived SHA lists sit on the same writable volume as the binaries, so they cannot prove the flashed image was the reviewed one.

## Evidence (live, 2026-10-19)
2026-10-19 read-only source and live readback, verdify-platform main aa93a521. firmware/greenhouse.yaml protects the device only with `ota: - platform: esphome, password: !secret ota_password` and `api: encryption: key: !secret api_encryption_key`. No esp32 secure_boot, flash-encryption or signed-app-verification option appears anywhere in firmware/. scripts/firmware-rollback.sh line 8-9 says it uses espota2 'to flash an arbitrary .ota.bin over the network', so the device accepts any image presented with the password. scripts/archive-firmware-artifacts.sh writes only sha256 lists (SHA256SUMS, SOURCE_SHA256SUMS, BUILD_SHA256SUMS) on the same RWO PVC verdify-firmware-artifacts; there is no signature or attestation. The CronJob verdify-firmware-builder (deploy/k8s/components/firmware-builder/firmware-builder.yaml) has FW_REVISION default 'main', a mutable branch. It clones with a GitHub token, compiles with ESPHome/PlatformIO packages downloaded at run time, and with FLASH=1 runs `esphome upload` of the binary it just compiled, not a previously archived and reviewed artifact. The same pod holds the OTA password, the device API PSK, the WLAN SSID and passphrase, and the GitHub token. NetworkPolicy allow-firmware-builder-egress allows egress to ipBlock 0.0.0.0/0 with no except, which covers the internet and every LAN VLAN. The original auditor recorded one TCP connect check from the operator Mac (VLAN 40) succeeding on 3232 and 6053; network-infra#42 asks for passive evidence only, so the verifier did not repeat it and the acceptance below requires passive readback. Related open issues: verdify-platform#390 gates releases on behaviour and notes 'live flash bytes were not hashed; the matching archive/provenance directory is absent'. network-infra#42 and #77 cover narrowing the ingestor-to-device 6053 allow. None covers image signing, device-side verification, the mutable-ref flash path or OTA port 3232 reachability.

Affected: `device:greenhouse ESP32 192.168.10.111 (greenhouse.devices.vallery.net) OTA tcp/3232, native API tcp/6053`, `k8s:verdify-prod/cronjob/verdify-firmware-builder`, `k8s:verdify-prod/networkpolicy/allow-firmware-builder-egress`, `k8s:verdify-prod/pvc/verdify-firmware-artifacts`, `k8s:verdify-prod/secret/verdify-firmware-ota`, `k8s:verdify-prod/secret/verdify-app-secrets:ESP32_API_KEY`, `k8s:verdify-prod/secret/verdify-firmware-wifi`, `repo:VerdifyConsultancy/verdify-platform:firmware/greenhouse.yaml`, `repo:VerdifyConsultancy/verdify-platform:scripts/firmware-rollback.sh`

## Approach
1) Builder: require FW_REVISION to be a full 40-char SHA (fail on a branch name). Pin PlatformIO platform and package versions in greenhouse.yaml. Split compile and flash into separate Job templates: compile archives firmware.ota.bin plus a cosign signature (sign-blob with a KSOPS-held key, or keyless in-cluster) and an in-toto provenance file. The flash job takes an artifact version, runs `cosign verify-blob` and checks SHA256SUMS before espota2 upload. 2) Device: enable ESP-IDF 'Require signed app images' (CONFIG_SECURE_SIGNED_APPS_NO_SECURE_BOOT with the matching signing key, via esphome esp32 framework sdkconfig_options), so OTA rejects unsigned binaries. Evaluate Secure Boot v2 separately because it is irreversible on the chip, and record the decision. 3) Rotate ota_password after signing is in place, and keep it only in verdify-firmware-ota. 4) Replace the builder egress 0.0.0.0/0 with the registry/GitHub/PlatformIO CIDRs it needs plus 192.168.10.111/32:3232, using `except` for the RFC1918 ranges. 5) Network (network-infra#42/#77): allow 3232/6053 to the device only from the builder and ingestor egress identities, and deny the home and other VLANs. Per network-infra#42, verify passively, not with connect canaries.

## Alignment with best practice and estate rules
NIST SP 800-193 (platform firmware resiliency: authenticated update); NIST IR 8259A device cybersecurity capability 'software update'; ETSI EN 303 645 provision 5.3 (secure software updates); SLSA Build L2 provenance. Estate R14; STD-CI-04.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The firmware-builder CronJob rejects a non-SHA FW_REVISION, and compile output includes a signature and a provenance file beside SHA256SUMS on the artifacts PVC
- [ ] The flash job verifies the signature and refuses an artifact whose signature fails (shown with a harmless tampered fixture, not on the live device)
- [ ] firmware/greenhouse.yaml enables signed-app verification, or a recorded Jason decision explains why it is deferred and what compensates
- [ ] allow-firmware-builder-egress no longer contains an unrestricted 0.0.0.0/0 rule
- [ ] UniFi policy readback shows tcp/3232 and tcp/6053 to 192.168.10.111 allowed only from the named builder and ingestor sources (verified passively per network-infra#42)
- [ ] ota_password rotated after cutover, with a metadata-only receipt

## Dependencies
jvallery/network-infra#42, jvallery/network-infra#77, VerdifyConsultancy/verdify-platform#390


## Decision needed from Jason

Yes. This finding needs Jason's decision or explicit go before execution (data, credentials, exposure, cost or downtime).

_Filed by the 2026-10-19 estate best-practice gap audit. The finding was verified live by an independent re-check. Baseline: [docs/estate/STANDARDS.md](https://github.com/jvallery/agents/blob/main/docs/estate/STANDARDS.md); owner from the estate ownership record (jvallery/agents `registry/policy/estate-ownership/`)._

<!-- planning-status:start -->
## Planning status (2026-10-19)

### Status (2026-10-19)
Not started; awaits decision on device-side verification.
### Evidence
- Static OTA password only
- Related network-infra#42/#77, #390 open
### Acceptance
- Satisfied: none yet
- Outstanding: builder rejects non-SHA, emits signature+provenance; flash verifies signature (tampered fixture); signed-app verification or recorded decision; no 0.0.0.0/0 egress; UniFi 3232/6053 narrowed (passive); ota_password rotated
### Related work
#390 (release gate), network-infra#42/#77
### Dependencies
UniFi criterion depends on network-infra#77 (sequencing).
### Priority & next action
P2: Get Jason's decision on device-side signing; implement SHA-only builder + signed artifacts + narrowed egress first. Verify: tampered-fixture refusal; NetworkPolicy readback.
### Standard
STD-CI-04, R14
### Triage (2026-10-20)
- Priority: **P2**. Device accepts any OTA with one static password from any routed VLAN; real but requires credential/LAN access; needs Jason's device-signing decision.
- Quality: Split: (a) builder SHA-only + egress narrowing (no decision needed, do now) from (b) device-side signed-app verification (Jason decision, irreversible risks).
- Decision (Jason, 2026-10-20, DR-48): Jason deferred device-side signed-app verification and approved compensating controls instead: an OTA-port network ACL limited to the CI/builder source plus OTA password rotation.
<!-- planning-status:end -->

body:
**Estate audit EST-AUD-224**: severity **medium**, dimension `security-exposure`, standard [STD-EXP-02](https://github.com/jvallery/agents/blob/main/docs/estate/STANDARDS.md#std-exp-02)

## What needs to change
Anonymous public reads on api.verdify.ai, including a camera proxy that reaches the family's production Frigate NVR, have no rate limit at Cloudflare, at either Traefik tier or in the app. Several anonymous list endpoints accept an unbounded limit or days value, and the contact form runs without Turnstile. (Unauthenticated POST /mcp traffic on mcp.verdify.ai is left to R4-external-mcp-and-ai-connector-ingress-03, which puts edge pre-auth in front of that host.)

## Why it matters
The public API is anonymous by design, but nothing caps load. A single client looping on latest.jpg makes the home security NVR decode and resize a 1080p frame for every request. A request such as observations/recent?limit=10000000 lets an anonymous caller run large scans on the production TimescaleDB that the greenhouse controller depends on. Auth failures on mcp.verdify.ai are never throttled. The contact form, which sends email, relies on a per-IP counter alone because Turnstile is not configured.

## Evidence (live, 2026-10-19)
2026-10-19 ~22:20Z read-only. Cloudflare API v4 GETs on zone verdify.ai used the network-infra read token, decoded in process and never printed. They returned 404 (code 10003) for /rulesets/phases/http_ratelimit/entrypoint and for http_request_firewall_custom, and /rate_limits (legacy) is empty. The only non-managed ruleset is http_request_cache_settings. Traefik: the only Middleware on routes verdify-t2-api, -lab and -mcp is verdify-strip-identity-headers. No RateLimit or InFlightReq middleware exists in verdify-prod, although rateLimit middlewares exist elsewhere (network-infra/rate-limit, network-infra/web-ratelimit, options-tracker/options-rate-limit, agent-fleet-ci/github-webhook-rate-limit). App: anonymous `GET /api/v1/public/cameras/{greenhouse_1|greenhouse_2}/latest.jpg?h<=1080` calls `_fetch_camera_snapshot_sync` through asyncio.to_thread on every request (api/main.py ~3571). That fetch goes to VERDIFY_FRIGATE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://frigate.frigate.svc.cluster.local:8971, the production home Frigate, using a bearer token. There is no response cache; one probe returned 315 KB in 1.28s. `GET /api/v1/observations/recent?limit=`, `/api/v1/crops/{id}/observations?limit=`, `/api/v1/crops/{id}/events?limit=` and `/api/v1/crops/{id}/health?days=` have no maximum in code or OpenAPI (main.py:2521 passes `limit` straight to `LIMIT $1`), unlike /crops (max 500) and band-trace/gpu-power (max 168h). The contact form has a per-IP limit (5/h, keyed on CF-Connecting-IP) but VERDIFY_TURNSTILE_SECRET is not set on the Deployment, so `_verify_turnstile_if_configured` skips the check. The verdify-api container limit is 2 CPU / 1Gi. The 24h access log on one verdify-traefik replica shows 3,264 unauthenticated `POST /mcp` 401s (~136/h, unthrottled) and 206 latest.jpg fetches. R2 finding network-infra#734 covers the managed WAF/OWASP rulesets only; it does not cover rate limiting. No open verdify-platform issue matches 'rate limit', 'turnstile' or 'api.verdify.ai' other than #1002 (graphs).

Affected: `hostname:api.verdify.ai`, `k8s:verdify-prod/deployment/verdify-api`, `k8s:verdify-prod/ingressroute/verdify-t2-api`, `k8s:frigate/service/frigate:8971`, `external-service:cloudflare/zone/verdify.ai (http_ratelimit phase)`, `repo:VerdifyConsultancy/verdify-platform:api/main.py`

## Approach
1) App (smallest change): add a `le=` bound to every unbounded limit/days query parameter, for example limit<=500 and days<=365. Cache latest.jpg per (camera, h) for 10-30s, as the existing _PUBLIC_*_CACHE dicts do, and bound concurrent Frigate fetches with a semaphore. 2) Traefik tier 2: add a RateLimit middleware (average/burst per source using the CF-Connecting-IP header via sourceCriterion.requestHeaderName) and an InFlightReq middleware to verdify-t2-api, with a tighter limit on /api/v1/public/cameras (key on Cf-Connecting-Ip only for requests arriving from the tier-1 forward; see R4-ingress-edge-headers-and-admin-route-restriction-01 for the trusted-source pattern). 3) Ask network-infra to add an http_ratelimit rule on verdify.ai for api.verdify.ai/api/v1/public/cameras/* (Pro plan supports it), declared in network-infra Cloudflare source next to #734. 4) Provision VERDIFY_TURNSTILE_SECRET through KSOPS and have www send the token, or document why the contact form stays without it.

## Alignment with best practice and estate rules
OWASP API Security Top 10 2023 API4 (Unrestricted Resource Consumption); OWASP ASVS V11.1.4 (anti-automation); NIST SP 800-53 SC-5. Estate R2, R3; STD-EXP-02.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] OpenAPI at https://api.verdify.ai/openapi.json shows a maximum on limit for /api/v1/observations/recent, /api/v1/crops/{crop_id}/observations, /api/v1/crops/{crop_id}/events and on days for /api/v1/crops/{crop_id}/health
- [ ] Two latest.jpg requests within the cache TTL (including with an extra unknown query parameter) produce one Frigate fetch, shown in the api log or Frigate access log
- [ ] A burst of 50 requests in 10s from one client to /api/v1/public/cameras/greenhouse_1/latest.jpg gets 429 after the configured burst while verdify.ai and lab.verdify.ai page loads stay 200
- [ ] IngressRoute verdify-t2-api lists RateLimit and InFlightReq middlewares in Git and live, Argo Synced
- [ ] GET /zones/{verdify.ai}/rulesets/phases/http_ratelimit/entrypoint returns 200 with the camera rule declared in network-infra source, or a recorded decision not to use the edge layer
- [ ] verdify-api env shows VERDIFY_TURNSTILE_SECRET from a Secret, or OWNERSHIP.md records the decision to run the contact form without it

## Dependencies
jvallery/network-infra#734


_Filed by the 2026-10-19 estate best-practice gap audit. The finding was verified live by an independent re-check. Baseline: [docs/estate/STANDARDS.md](https://github.com/jvallery/agents/blob/main/docs/estate/STANDARDS.md); owner from the estate ownership record (jvallery/agents `registry/policy/estate-ownership/`)._

<!-- planning-status:start -->
## Planning status (2026-10-19)

### Status (2026-10-19)
Not started.
### Evidence
- No rate-limit middleware in verdify-prod
- network-infra#734 open
### Acceptance
- Satisfied: none yet
- Outstanding: OpenAPI maxima on limit/days; latest.jpg cache; 429 after burst; RateLimit/InFlightReq in Git and live; edge rate-limit rule or decision; Turnstile secret or recorded decision
### Related work
network-infra#734 (WAF, separate scope)
### Dependencies
Edge criterion sequenced with network-infra#734 (related, not hard).
### Priority & next action
P2: Ship app bounds + camera cache first (PR), then Traefik RateLimit/InFlightReq; ask network-infra for edge rule. Verify: openapi.json maxima; 50-request burst gets 429.
### Standard
STD-EXP-02, R2, R3
### Triage (2026-10-20)
- Priority: **P2**. Unbounded anonymous load on the prod DB and the home Frigate NVR (medium); app-side bounds and camera cache are cheap.
- Standards (corrected): STD-EXP-01
- Quality: STD-EXP-02 covers data-plane services (registry/logs/test endpoints); unbounded anonymous DB queries map better to STD-EXP-01 'no anonymous data-query paths'. No standard covers rate limits—note that gap.
<!-- planning-status:end -->

body:
**Estate audit EST-AUD-223**: severity **medium**, dimension `security-exposure`, standard [STD-EXP-01](https://github.com/jvallery/agents/blob/main/docs/estate/STANDARDS.md#std-exp-01)

## What needs to change
Decide whether any external client needs mcp.verdify.ai. If none, drop the public route (keep a probe on a /readyz path or in-cluster). If one does, require Cloudflare Access (service token or mTLS) on the hostname so the bearer token is a second factor, and issue that client its own audience token instead of reusing Iris's.

## Why it matters
A single long-lived shared secret, also mounted in the Hermes pod, is the only barrier between the internet and tools that change physical greenhouse setpoints and post to Slack. STD-EXP-01 requires edge pre-auth or MFA for internet-reachable apps.

## Evidence (live, 2026-10-19)
2026-10-19: public DNS (1.1.1.1) resolves mcp.verdify.ai to Cloudflare 104.26.8.72/104.26.9.72/172.67.70.122; curl via those IPs without a token returns the origin's 401 JSON with 'server: cloudflare', cf-ray and 'www-authenticate: Bearer' (no Cloudflare Access redirect/403, no OAuth metadata: /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource 404). Inside the LAN the name split-resolves to 192.168.7.10 (traefik-apps) and returns the same 401 from 'server: uvicorn'. IngressRoute verdify-t2-mcp: Host(mcp.verdify.ai) && PathPrefix(/mcp) -> verdify-mcp:8000 with only middleware verdify-strip-identity-headers; Cloudflare tunnel rule #9 forwards it (planning/reviews/2026-10-18-ingress-988). VERDIFY_MCP_AUTH_MODE=enforce; audiences are static env tokens (VERDIFY_MCP_TOKEN_IRIS from Secret verdify-hermes created 2026-06-07, VERDIFY_MCP_TOKEN_OBSERVER). The #988 receipt public-final-mcp.json shows the iris token over the public hostname lists 23 tools including set_plan, set_tunable (greenhouse setpoint writes), lessons_manage and slack_ops. The only production consumer, verdify-hermes-iris, uses the ClusterIP (config.yaml url http://verdify-mcp.verdify-prod.svc:8000/mcp); the endpoint-prober calls the public URL without a token and expects 401. mcp logs (24h, both pods) show about 15,800 mcp_transport_authn_denial events, and a small number of authenticated 200s (e.g. 4 in one pod) arriving via the verdify-traefik pods (10.42.4.121, 10.42.6.158), origin unknown; the rest come from verdify-hermes-iris 10.42.4.220.

Affected: `endpoint:mcp.verdify.ai`, `route:verdify-prod/verdify-t2-mcp`, `k8s:verdify-prod/deployment/verdify-mcp`, `k8s:verdify-prod/secret/verdify-hermes:VERDIFY_MCP_TOKEN`

## Approach
1) Check Cloudflare/Traefik logs for the 7 daily authenticated public calls to identify the client. 2) Either remove the route and DNS record or add a Cloudflare Access application with a service-token policy for mcp.verdify.ai (network-infra owns Access/DNS; verdify-platform owns the route). 3) Rotate the iris token afterwards since it has been usable publicly since June. 4) Update the endpoint-prober contract to the new expected status.

## Alignment with best practice and estate rules
R2/R3 public hostnames go through Cloudflare with pre-auth; route owner verdify-platform, Access policy via network-infra.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An unauthenticated request to https://mcp.verdify.ai/mcp is rejected by Cloudflare Access (or the hostname no longer resolves to a route)
- [ ] The iris token presented without the Access credential is rejected at the edge
- [ ] verdify-hermes-iris still lists its tools over the ClusterIP
- [ ] Iris token rotated with readback of Secret metadata only


## Decision needed from Jason

Yes. This finding needs Jason's decision or explicit go before execution (data, credentials, exposure, cost or downtime).

_Filed by the 2026-10-19 estate best-practice gap audit. The finding was verified live by an independent re-check. Baseline: [docs/estate/STANDARDS.md](https://github.com/jvallery/agents/blob/main/docs/estate/STANDARDS.md); owner from the estate ownership record (jvallery/agents `registry/policy/estate-ownership/`)._

<!-- planning-status:start -->
## Planning status (2026-10-19)

### Status (2026-10-19)
Not started; awaits Jason decision (remove route vs Access).
### Evidence
- Public 401 from origin, no edge pre-auth

**Estate audit EST-AUD-218**: severity **high**, dimension `security-k8s`, standard [STD-K8S-02](https://github.com/jvallery/agents/blob/main/docs/estate/STANDARDS.md#std-k8s-02)

## What needs to change
Replace the verdify-traefik ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding with a Role and RoleBinding in verdify-prod covering only services, endpoints, endpointslices and the traefik.io CRDs it watches. Remove Secret access. Remove configmaps and nodes unless a startup test shows Traefik v3.7 needs them.

## Why it matters
This pod is the first in-cluster hop for every anonymous internet request to the Verdify product hosts. A Traefik RCE, a dependency compromise or a token leak would give the attacker read access to every Secret in the estate, including the root B2 management key, Cloudflare and network credentials, Authentik and database passwords, from a pod that only needs to route five hostnames inside one namespace. Scanners are already probing it for the service-account token path. R18 also says app repos install no cluster-wide controller.

## Evidence (live, 2026-10-19)
2026-10-19 ~22:30Z read-only. Live ClusterRole verdify-traefik grants get/list/watch on core services, endpoints, secrets, configmaps and nodes cluster-wide, plus endpointslices and the traefik.io CRDs; ClusterRoleBinding verdify-traefik binds it to SA verdify-prod/verdify-traefik. The source is deploy/k8s/overlays/prod/traefik/verdify-traefik-rbac.yaml lines 30-43 at verdify-platform main aa93a521. `kubectl auth can-i list secrets -A --as=system:serviceaccount:verdify-prod:verdify-traefik` = yes, and `get secrets -n auth` = yes. The cluster holds 936 Secrets in 84 namespaces, including storage-infra/b2-root-management (the all-bucket B2 key that can manage keys) and network-infra/network-infra-credentials. The Deployment does not need this access: it runs docker.io/traefik:v3.7.1 with --providers.kubernetescrd.namespaces=verdify-prod and labelselector traefik-tier=verdify; its only entryPoint, verdify-web, is plain HTTP on :8000 with no TLS; and its only Middleware is verdify-strip-identity-headers, a headers middleware that reads no Secret. automountServiceAccountToken is unset, so the pod has a token. Every public request to api, lab, labs, mcp and graphs.verdify.ai passes through this pod (tier-1 route verdify-prod/verdify-tier1-forward sends every *.verdify.ai host to it). Its access log for the last 24h on one replica shows 41,646 requests: 22,902 were 404s and about 11.8k matched scanner patterns, including `GET /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token` and `/@fs/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token?raw??`. Open issue verdify-platform#995 only records the ClusterRole as an owned cluster-scoped object ('R18 check recorded'); it does not narrow it. No prior audit finding names verdify-traefik RBAC (security-k8s-11 covers kube-state-metrics only).

Affected: `k8s:clusterrole/verdify-traefik`, `k8s:clusterrolebinding/verdify-traefik`, `k8s:verdify-prod/serviceaccount/verdify-traefik`, `k8s:verdify-prod/deployment/verdify-traefik`, `repo:VerdifyConsultancy/verdify-platform:deploy/k8s/overlays/prod/traefik/verdify-traefik-rbac.yaml`, `hostnames: api.verdify.ai, lab.verdify.ai, labs.verdify.ai, mcp.verdify.ai, graphs.verdify.ai`

## Approach
1) In deploy/k8s/overlays/prod/traefik/verdify-traefik-rbac.yaml, change kind ClusterRole to Role (namespace verdify-prod) with rules: core services, endpoints; discovery.k8s.io endpointslices; traefik.io ingressroutes, middlewares, traefikservices, serverstransports, tlsoptions and tlsstores (get, list, watch). Bind it with a RoleBinding. 2) Delete the ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding by exact name after Argo syncs the Role, and update the agents estate-ownership kubernetes-cluster-scoped.yaml entries (verdify-traefik under clusterrole and clusterrolebinding) to drop them. 3) If a future TLS or basicAuth middleware needs a Secret, grant get on that Secret by resourceNames only. 4) Add a repo test that fails if any verdify-platform RBAC object grants secrets list or watch outside a namespaced Role with resourceNames. 5) Check the verdify-traefik logs for 'forbidden' after rollout and check that api/lab/labs/mcp return their current status codes.

## Alignment with best practice and estate rules
CIS Kubernetes Benchmark 5.1.2 (minimize access to secrets) and 5.1.3; NIST SP 800-53 AC-6; Traefik docs: with providers.kubernetescrd.namespaces set, namespaced RBAC is enough. Estate R5, R18, R21; STD-K8S-02.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `kubectl auth can-i list secrets -A --as=system:serviceaccount:verdify-prod:verdify-traefik` returns no, and `get secrets -n verdify-prod` returns no
- [ ] `kubectl get clusterrole,clusterrolebinding verdify-traefik` returns NotFound, and the agents estate-ownership cluster-scoped map no longer lists them
- [ ] api.verdify.ai/health and lab.verdify.ai return 200, mcp.verdify.ai/mcp returns 401 unauthenticated, and verdify-traefik logs show no RBAC 'forbidden' errors for 1h after rollout
- [ ] A repo check fails CI if a verdify-platform RBAC rule grants secrets list/watch

**Estate audit EST-AUD-158**: severity **low**, dimension `ha-spof`, standard [STD-HA-02](https://github.com/jvallery/agents/blob/main/docs/estate/STANDARDS.md#std-ha-02)

## What needs to change
Both replicas mount one RWO PVC and the pod template carries a required podAffinity to the portable-rwo cache cohort on kubernetes.io/hostname, so both pods are forced onto the same node (node5); the soft spread constraint cannot separate them.

## Why it matters
Blast radius: node5 loss takes down verdify-lab entirely despite replicas=2 and a PDB, so the PDB and replica count give false assurance.

## Evidence (live, 2026-10-19)
Verifier re-check 2026-10-19 ~14:55 local (read-only): `kubectl get deploy verdify-lab -n verdify-prod -o json` -> replicas 2, both Running pods on vm-k3s-node5; pod template has REQUIRED podAffinity (requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution, labelSelector verdify.ai/lab-cache-cohort=portable-rwo, topologyKey kubernetes.io/hostname) plus topologySpreadConstraints whenUnsatisfiable=ScheduleAnyway; PVC verdify-lab-site-cache (pvc-1bd6ffec) RWO, 2 Longhorn replicas node5+node7, attached node5; PDB verdify-lab minAvailable=1 disruptionsAllowed=1.

Affected: `k8s-workload:verdify-prod/deployment/verdify-lab`, `pvc:verdify-prod/verdify-lab-site-cache`

## Approach
Make the site cache per-pod (emptyDir rebuilt at start, or volumeClaimTemplates via a StatefulSet) or RWX; then remove the required podAffinity to the portable-rwo cohort and set the hostname spread constraint to DoNotSchedule (or required podAntiAffinity).

## Alignment with best practice and estate rules
Kubernetes topology spread guidance; Google SRE redundancy. Estate R10.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] verdify-lab Running pods are on two distinct nodes (`kubectl get pods -n verdify-prod -l app.kubernetes.io/component=lab-site -o wide`)
- [ ] No required podAffinity on kubernetes.io/hostname remains in the verdify-lab pod template
- [ ] Deleting either pod leaves one Ready replica serving the lab site (HTTP 200 throughout)

**Estate audit EST-AUD-108**: severity **medium**, dimension `cicd`, standard [STD-CI-01](https://github.com/jvallery/agents/blob/main/docs/estate/STANDARDS.md#std-ci-01)

## What needs to change
Production promotions and most code changes land on main by direct push with no CI of any kind; the repo's PR CI never sees them, and verdify-prod-dark renders straight from main.

## Why it matters
Unvalidated changes, including prod image pins, reach the production overlay; a bad pin or manifest is caught only at sync time. There is no CI record tying a deployed revision to a green check, so a rollback target cannot be chosen from evidence. Unsigned direct pushes to a public repo also weaken provenance.

## Evidence (live, 2026-10-19)
gh api 'repos/VerdifyConsultancy/verdify-platform/commits?sha=main&since=2026-10-12T00:00:00Z&per_page=100' -> 100 commits, 91 unsigned; gh pr list --state merged --search 'merged:>=2026-10-12' -> 13 PRs. Last 20 main commits: 19 unsigned, 19 with no associated PR (gh api repos/.../commits/<sha>/pulls -> []). Release commit 7fc3956d 'release(api): promote authenticated public camera reader for #988' (2026-10-19, changes only deploy/k8s/overlays/prod/release-pins.yaml) has 0 commit statuses and 0 check runs; same for 280a3239 and 7e86ca14. Main HEAD aa93a521 statuses=[]. Only PR heads get 'Verdify Platform / Argo PR CI'. Branch protection on main: linear history only, no required checks (gh api repos/.../branches/main/protection). Repo is public. kubectl get applications: verdify-prod-dark source deploy/k8s/overlays/prod @ main. [verify: reproduced; severity lowered high->medium: CI/change-control gap, not active exposure, SPOF or missing backup/alert]

Affected: `VerdifyConsultancy/verdify-platform main`, `deploy/k8s/overlays/prod/release-pins.yaml`, `Argo app verdify-prod-dark (targetRevision main, manual sync)`

## Approach
1) Run the existing platform validation (registry ci_submission steps / 'Argo PR CI') on push to main as well, posting a commit status on every main SHA. 2) Make release-pin promotion a PR (or a bot-authored PR from the release tool) so 'Argo PR CI' gates it. 3) Once main pushes are reliably validated, ask agents to add that context as a required check in config/branch-protection-baseline.yml for this repo (strict=false per D14). 4) Treat the commit status on the promoted SHA as the precondition for syncing verdify-prod-dark.

## Alignment with best practice and estate rules
OpenGitOps principles 1-2 (declarative, versioned and immutable: changes via reviewed and validated Git history); SLSA v1.0 Source track (verified change history); NIST SP 800-53 CM-3/CM-4 (change control, impact analysis); estate R14 (digest pin committed by the owning repo) and R17 (one check entrypoint every gate calls).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every commit on main after the change has a CI commit status (gh api repos/VerdifyConsultancy/verdify-platform/commits/<sha>/status shows a context).
- [ ] Changes to deploy/k8s/overlays/prod/release-pins.yaml arrive by merged PR with a green 'Argo PR CI' (or successor) status on the head SHA.
- [ ] A 7-day sample shows 0 main commits without an associated PR or a main-push validation status.


## Decision needed from Jason

Yes. This finding needs Jason's decision or explicit go before execution (data, credentials, exposure, cost or downtime).

**Estate audit EST-AUD-029**: severity **high**, dimension `security-exposure`, standard [STD-EXP-01](https://github.com/jvallery/agents/blob/main/docs/estate/STANDARDS.md#std-exp-01)

## What needs to change
Anonymous viewers can send arbitrary raw SQL to the production TimescaleDB datasource via /api/ds/query (Grafana Viewer can query any datasource it can see). Public telemetry should be served without granting ad-hoc query capability.

## Why it matters
Any internet client can read every table/view the Grafana DB role can SELECT (beyond what dashboards show) and run expensive queries (pg_sleep, large scans) against the production greenhouse database, a confidentiality and availability risk; it also bypasses dashboard-level curation of what is public.

## Evidence (live, 2026-10-19)
2026-10-19 forced-public path (curl --resolve graphs.verdify.ai:443:<CF IP>): GET /api/frontend/settings -> Grafana 12.4.5, anonymousEnabled=true, datasource 'TimescaleDB (Verdify)' type grafana-postgresql-datasource; GET /api/search -> 28 dashboards anonymously; POST /api/ds/query {rawSql:'SELECT 1 AS probe'} with no credentials -> status 200, values [[1]]; follow-up read-only SELECT of current_user -> verdify_grafana_runtime_login, rolsuper=false, 0 direct INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grants. kubectl get deploy -A env: verdify-prod/verdify-grafana GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=true, GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ORG_ROLE=Viewer. Route verdify-prod/verdify-tier1-forward and tunnel wildcard *.verdify.ai expose it publicly. | 2026-10-19 verify re-run: curl --resolve graphs.verdify.ai:443:172.67.70.122 /api/frontend/settings -> anonymousEnabled=true, Grafana 12.4.5, datasource 'TimescaleDB (Verdify)' grafana-postgresql-datasource; GET /api/search -> 200; anonymous POST /api/ds/query rawSql 'SELECT 1 AS probe' -> status 200 values [[1]]; kubectl -n verdify-prod get deploy verdify-grafana env GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=true, GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ORG_ROLE=Viewer. Owner: endpoint:graphs.verdify.ai backend+route owner VerdifyConsultancy/verdify-platform (edge.yaml). No open issue (searched 'grafana anonymous', 'graphs.verdify.ai').

Affected: `endpoint:graphs.verdify.ai`, `k8s:verdify-prod/deployment/verdify-grafana`, `grafana-datasource:TimescaleDB (Verdify)`

## Approach
1) Disable anonymous auth (GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=false) and publish the intended public panels through Grafana Public/Shared Dashboards (which only execute the saved panel queries) or through the existing public API endpoints on api.verdify.ai. 2) If anonymous must remain briefly, put the datasource behind a dedicated read-only role limited to curated views with statement_timeout and row limits, and remove datasource query permission for the anonymous org via datasource permissions. 3) Re-probe /api/ds/query anonymously after rollout.

## Alignment with best practice and estate rules
OWASP Top 10 A01 Broken Access Control; NIST SP 800-53 AC-3/AC-6 (least privilege), CSF PR.AA; CIS Controls 3.3 (data access control). Estate R3 (route/backend owner owns its exposure) and R13 boundary (dashboards in an app namespace are app-owned).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Anonymous POST https://graphs.verdify.ai/api/ds/query via the public Cloudflare path returns 401/403
- [ ] Intended public dashboards remain viewable via public-dashboard links or the public API
- [ ] Grafana DB role has statement_timeout set and SELECT only on curated public views (readback of grants)

Campaign: #775 · Stage: **C4 — Delivery and runtime reliability** · Priority: P1 · Effort: S · Accountable role: Data/platform lead.

October19 05:23 UTC dependency refresh: Home Assistant #878 closed COMPLETED at04:27:44 after PR#894, merged ff250799a553262317ee8802c72682422fb6d398. Its accepted installed-source contract qualifies authentic per-channel update time and power from the existing enabled read-only Modbus endpoint, including advancing stable0W. Native HA representation clocks do not expose this provenance; existing consumer stale denial and NULL aggregate remain correct. No HA runtime/configuration change was needed. Source contract: https://github.com/jvallery/homeassistant/blob/ff250799a553262317ee8802c72682422fb6d398/docs/operations/SHELLY_SOURCE_CLOCK.md; evidence: https://github.com/jvallery/homeassistant/blob/ff250799a553262317ee8802c72682422fb6d398/docs/home/evidence/source-clock-20261018/README.md.

Do not substitute observation/fetch/ingest time for source time, reinterpret reversed channel1 CT or partial-circuit coverage, infer scientific eligibility, repeat accepted owner probes or invent a new credential/network route. The native predecessor link is retained as closed history. No #981 implementation or production source read was performed by the #988 repair.

Prior dated evidence, retained unchanged:

The bounded source/ingestion comparison at 02:05 UTC and four read-only Shelly RPCs at 02:11 UTC on October 18 completed with zero mutations. At those observations, intended channel 0 read zero watts while HA last_updated and last_reported remained 2026-10-17T23:53:51Z; ingestion truthfully marked it stale after 300 seconds and denied the aggregate with null watts_total. Channel 1 source time advanced and its reversed-CT/partial-circuit negative value was preserved. Device system time and an available zero reading do not establish an advancing per-channel sample clock or prove an HA defect. The 06:59:54 UTC native graph still records open jvallery/homeassistant#878 as the single external blocker. The 07:07 product smoke passed, but it does not qualify that source clock or grant energy eligibility. Trace and recover the stale energy source while preserving honest channel quality.

Recent database rows can carry old underlying source values, invalidating scientific/resource claims.

2. If owner qualification demonstrates a defect, repair it in the actual owning lane; otherwise retain the documented upstream constraint. Keep source and ingestion clocks distinct and preserve intended identities and reversed-CT semantics.

October 4 custom/generic calls returned the same four 46-column rows in 11.269874/4.966761 seconds: two complete/ineffective and two incomplete/insufficient-evidence, none effective. These are installed-production timings within the unchanged 15-second fence; the 3.174204-second clone result is not a production timing. Original failures, twenty native full-row parity fixtures, 2,673 genuine clone readback relations, installed ledger/seal/receipt and prior runtime evidence remain unchanged.

A new single bounded read-only assessment of the complete selected stored input found incomplete recorded solar-day coverage on both dates. October 16 has 644 of 669 valid recorded minutes, 25 missing clock buckets, zero known held-admission minutes and 12 ordinary dehumidification minutes. October 17 has 643 of 666, 23 missing clock buckets, zero known held-admission minutes and 2 ordinary dehumidification minutes. The 48 missing clock buckets are not interpolated or counted twice across climate/action records. Complete-recorded-daytime measured-zero remains NULL on both dates; no historical row was changed and continuous physical absence is not proved.

The optional default-off Iris scorecard reader from b814f35e is delivered at MCP digest ae8a367035a3ae8a06ab2384bc166f444b3decad0da21e5c70e53e76203d9c73. An explicit solar-night start date requests one bounded existing-getter read, preserving all 46 fields, NULLs, dispositions and confounds under the 500-episode/64-KiB limit. Iris retains 23 tools and outcome_kpi remains admin-only. The source-owned SOUL/inventory refresh is accepted; it requests prior-completed-night ordinary SUNRISE/SUNSET use.

The separately authorized GPT-6 Luna/xhigh profile and truthful API label are delivered from source 56b316f3fda666b25665dfc0f791d6be6db0fa46. The profile is 2261f5c1a236202b3bfccedd82f1284f50ab27445767dcb09439a92a8d58b56b; installed prompt/playbook/inventory prose remains unchanged, including legacy model-name text. No new natural cycle was launched; natural-cycle cost and the 20% comparison baseline remain unknown.

Two actual bounded ordinary-consumer cases passed using GPT-6 Luna/xhigh over Responses and the existing Iris audience. October 4 returned the same four complete 46-field rows as the prior installed-production custom read: two ineffective and two insufficient-evidence, none effective. October 16 returned no episodes, pending safety and NULL daytime counts. The fixed structured scope statement and actual counts/NULLs passed; this is forced, bounded evidence consumption, not autonomous tool selection or a full Hermes gateway cycle.

Next action: Define a supported observation/freshness contract and collect a prospective complete recorded daytime window; preserve the incomplete October 16/17 history. Observe intended outcome consumption in a naturally scheduled ordinary planner cycle, separately from the accepted bounded read/model qualification. Measure that new cycle before comparing cost. Reuse the installed getter and accepted delivery; keep physical efficacy, crop sensing and crop safety on their own evidence.

Full #410 remains open: bounded source, runtime, ordinary read and model interpretation do not prove a natural planner cycle, complete daytime observation or physical efficacy.

Evidence: planning/reviews/2026-10-18-daytime-consumer/README.md. All acceptance clauses, states, parents, dependencies and original estimates remain unchanged.

Define the observation/freshness contract for a prospectively collected complete recorded window; preserve ordinary daytime dehumidification and all solar, heat2, wind/dwell and temperature safeguards.
4. Reuse accepted actual Iris HTTP, source-owned Hermes refresh and separately bounded GPT-6 Luna interpretation. Observe a naturally scheduled ordinary-planner cycle separately and measure its cost before comparing. Preserve the distinction between safety, efficacy, incomplete coverage and crop safety; no universal VPD target or tuning follows.

Roles name execution responsibilities and preserve existing assignees. This contract supersedes conflicting historical sequencing; prior comments and receipts remain evidence.

## Current state and next action

S3B P4 completed the shared release-custody matrix: actual firmware version is sampled, a matching-version local binary and older copies are hashed, and current available heap pairs meet existing floors. Live flash bytes were not hashed; the matching archive/provenance directory is absent beside the inspected local copy. Copied metadata and filenames do not re-establish bake, topology/configuration compatibility or actual recovery. No artifact was promoted or flashed.

Reuse #985 strict native/invariants, 154 causal YAML cases, zero-divergence replay and both secretless compiler targets within their original source scope. Dummy-credential outputs remain NONDEPLOYABLE. #303/#304 tooling and #419 freshness acceptance remain retained, but exact operational candidate/binary, physical relay/configuration, representative runtime and recovery acceptance are still required for a selected release.

Current execution allocation: RELEASE. Next action: Reuse completed P4 shared custody and #985 compiler/causal/replay receipts. Resolve exact candidate/topology/configuration, live binary provenance, independently available recovery evidence and predeclared runtime canaries for a selected release. The matching-version local binary is retained, but missing adjacent archive/bake/recovery evidence prevents treating it as newly qualified last-good. No OTA in S3B.

Evidence: planning/reviews/2026-10-18-s3b-execution/p4-passive-heap/README.md. Existing acceptance clauses, issue state and completion edges are unchanged.

## What

Provide the reusable release gate for every later firmware OTA, including maintained topology, cycling semantics and real device acceptance.

## Why

Replay-only parity and short uptime miss relay misrouting, outdoor-blind paths, re-fire regressions and chronic heap/watchdog failures.

## How / implementation strategy

1. Reuse P4 exact known-artifact custody and existing compiler/replay receipts to assemble the selected candidate/topology/configuration/runtime packet. Resolve missing matching archive/provenance and actual recovery evidence without relabeling the retained copy as newly accepted last-good.
2. Bind independently available rollback bytes and pre/post canaries for one writer, resets/heap, climate guards, starts/dwell and affected irrigation routing. A provisional candidate stays explicitly unbaked; S3B performs no OTA.
3. Define observation duration and pass/fail thresholds before release; consume #428 bounded uncertainty and #299/#434 safety contracts for affected changes.

None beyond normal scoped delivery; this planning campaign authorizes no physical experiment or OTA.

Campaign: #775 · Stage: **C7 — Physical and seasonal commissioning** · Priority: P2 · Effort: M · Accountable role: Operator with data/control lead.

Full issue review, October 18, 2026. Delivery state: SEASONAL DECISION AWAITS OBSERVATIONS.

Completed or retained scope: The generic orchid-wide dormancy/calendar premise has been superseded by species-specific observational scope. No new crop condition evidence supports a dormancy/light/dry-down change. Source configuration cannot establish current species or seasonal need.

Remaining actual acceptance: A documented no-change or specific seasonal-care decision is supported by actual crop observations.; Any new dormancy/light/dry-down setting is versioned, reversible and cannot silently alter a locked study.; No species-wide agronomic or yield claim is made from uncalibrated DLI or a house-average proxy.

Current execution allocation: PHYSICAL. Next action: Use the shared field observations to record a finite no-change decision or one specific reversible seasonal-care action with its basis and study-intervention handling.

Full review: planning/reviews/2026-10-18-status/README.md. Existing acceptance clauses and actual completion edges are unchanged.

## What

Evaluate whether actual orchid species and observed stage warrant a dormancy flag, lighting clamp or dry-down governance this season.

## Why

A generic dormant-orchid row and universal 11–13-hour clamp can be wrong for the crop; old planning assumptions were explicitly conditional on empirical observations.

## How / implementation strategy

1. Use the shared #298 field inventory when available to record species and current condition; obtain a finite no-change or one reversible seasonal-care decision. Close on that documented decision instead of leaving a perpetual annual implementation ticket.
2. If justified, design typed stage/validity/provenance and bounded species-specific lighting/dry-down policy with missing-data fallback.
3. Keep the existing safe behavior until the seasonal evidence and release scope are accepted; coordinate with #410/#386 without using air VPD as root hydration proof.
